title: Review outcomes must reach every retained repair baseline
body: An initially clean baseline can later report the same advisory as new while another owns it as original. Apply assessments by stable finding identity to both without deleting raw evidence. Share current audits across baselines; verify each original scope and history. Sequential hooks may reuse complete audits, but skipped checks must retry. Never reuse approval outcomes solely from the current audit fingerprint: a review can cover an ignored path no longer mentioned in current docs. That path can change without changing the current fingerprint, so recheck original history and assessments on every invocation. Keep raw check caching separate from review status and include review-record contents in publication fingerprints. Scope reviews to relevant document/manifest history so metadata and unrelated commits preserve them. Observe explicit ignored paths because Git misses them. Decision findings consume existing authorized decision reviews. Share document/source inventory and exact history reads only within one inspection; final validation must use a new inspection, and failed reads must retry. Reusing initial discovery for validation can hide new documents, source deletions or ignore changes. Automation owns the final full-input guard; standalone repairs retain their guards. Regressions cover these boundaries, retained baselines, final commits and concurrent changes; they do not establish semantic correctness or authenticated approval.

Keep raw check caching separate from review status, and include review-record contents in publication fingerprints so a concurrent assessment cannot publish stale closure. Explicit ignored-path presence needs its own observation because Git alone misses it.
